description: PS5 homebrew diagnostic payloads, a usermode GDB debugger, a kernel offset inspection backend, CLI and GDB/MI runbooks, native app build tooling, and host analysis utilities.
rules: Check the compatibility guide before using a payload; kernel capture requires the matching PS5 Pro 13.60 instrumentation and page map.
Distinguish a successful local build or host-side transfer from console runtime validation.
Send payloads once and preserve the raw capture and metadata sidecar; do not automatically retry after a timeout.

Classify a black or frozen console from ICMP ping plus a real send; host/session_health.py never connects to port 9021. Ping alive and loader refused is elfldr_dead (power-hold). Ping dead is kernel_unreachable (power-hold). Ping alive after a successful send with a black picture is loader_ready (resident-snapshot once). HDMI black plus two beeps is display_sync / Safe Mode.

For process-debugger tasks read DEBUGGER_RECOVERY, DEBUGGER_VALIDATION, DEBUGGER, DEBUGGER_AGENTS and DEBUGGER_PROTOCOL before live CLI work; current source and session evidence override stale snippets.
The process debugger attaches to one usermode PID and cannot trap kernel offset 0xcfc12; title IDs are not PIDs and arbitrary system/game attachment remains unvalidated.
Retail 13.60 Z2/Z4 data watchpoints remain disabled. PROCESS_DEBUGGER_KERNEL_DBREGS is retired and rejected; never deploy the historical PCB fallback into a kstuff session.

DEBUGGER_BACKEND.md documents target.h, the protocol-independent target_ops contract: numeric identity, maps, threads, memory, named core registers, stop events, breakpoints and execution. The singleton ptrace provider owns policy/restoration; rsp.c owns packet/register/error encoding and polls controller interrupts through target_wait; main.c owns listener cleanup. Discovery methods provide 13.60 process metadata, bounded SDK-format sysctl maps, SDK basename module lookup and optional read-only ptrace FS/GS/XSAVE banks. Missing selectors or incompatible layouts return errors with no kernel fallback; runtime availability is unvalidated. No automatic GDB memory-map/library feature is advertised. Native errno and signals are translated at the frontend boundary. This refactor adds no console validation or live kernel provider.

Hardware slots may already belong to kstuff. Preserve other owners and report ENOSPC for Z1; use Z0 software INT3 breakpoints instead. The test-child slot lease is not available for real applications.

All process-memory mutations now use verified transactions: ordinary writes, software-breakpoint planting/removal, hidden-step restore/replant and detach restoration. Failed writes restore the preimage or set memory_poisoned and block resume/detach. qPS5:capabilities reports source/LLVM fingerprint, firmware/server PID, implemented query mask and limits; the mask is not successful runtime probing and the fingerprint is not the ELF hash. DEBUGGER_OVERLAP.md records the pinned ps5debug-NG study; this debugger remains standalone and does not import ShellCore injection, attach-policy patches or PCB register access.

DEBUGGER_REPORTS.md describes read_memory_ranges/qPS5:readv (1-16 ranges, 1024 total bytes, exact per-range results and zeroed failures), qPS5:state provider-lifetime stop serials, and ps5-report on the existing GDB Python connection. Reports preserve raw stack/code/frame bytes, native errors, source/local-file hashes, before/after stop checks and selection-restoration state; RBP walks are heuristic, never verified unwinds. Offline debugger_analyze.py supports nibble/wildcard searches and pinned Capstone 5.0.7 x86-64 RIP-relative/direct-branch cross-references, with gaps, limits and unresolved indirect/segment dependencies explicit. No second client, automatic attach/resume, target writes or console validation is added. The target XML describes the existing 560-byte file with unavailable FP/SSE/padding; unsupported GDB FreeBSD ABI handlers remain a client limitation.

Software breakpoint memory writes commit shadows only after verified completion; failed partial writes restore prior bytes or poison further memory writes/resume and refuse detach that would run unrestored memory. Hidden step-over runs the hit LWP and auto-continues only after its verified trace stop; other signals/stops are reported. These paths are host-tested, not console-validated.
Use one RSP client and bounded execution; source docs/debugger/compat.gdb before connecting. A successful register readback is not evidence that a watchpoint fires.
Preserve existing user authorization, identify the current target/session, log commands and cleanup state, and do not automatically resend, reconnect, kill or reboot after a timeout.
Keep LLVM 18 and the standard Payload SDK build; gpubox is the recorded workspace build host. Do not substitute LLVM 23 or a research-runtime ELF.

For kernel-offset work read KERNEL_DEBUGGER.md: exec+0xcfc12 = text+0x38fc12 = data-0x9303ee only in the checked profile. The separate SDK backend inspects gated bytes; it implements no kernel trap, watchpoint, stop, step or resume. A dated probe is not console readiness or whole-kernel identity.

Kernel inspection readiness uses KERNEL_READINESS.md: default builds require an explicitly linked versioned provider; legacy-cookie fallback is opt-in and read-only. Never fall back after a malformed, stale, initializing, failed or changing handshake. Schema-2 evidence distinguishes readiness sources; existing residents are not automatically upgraded. Draft residents/readiness loader/service tests cover packed TSS fields and publication/revocation only, not a working installer or syscall transport.

KERNEL_PATCH_TOOLKIT_PLAN.md tracks the unfinished staged plan; KERNEL_PATCH_TOOLKIT.md documents the implemented offline manifest/policy generator, fixed C/Python wire codec and portable exact-policy patch core. make kernel-patch-host builds a host-only synthetic-memory simulator; make kernel-patch-check emits a freestanding SDK object, not an installer. Separate pinned identity/capabilities, a real target lease, verified apply/exercise/revert, preimage journaling, exact readback/restoration, replay and sticky poison are enforced by the core with trusted adapter callbacks. Existing inspection readiness grants no writes. The separate stage 2 source overlay supplies an authenticated inspection bridge; the separate stage 3 owned-cell source adapter implements only a dedicated test variable, with SDK installer integration/link and console validation outstanding; real selected kernel-data policies remain unfinished. Code mutation is explicitly refused pending hardware quiescence, instruction-flow review, instruction-stream synchronization and verified restoration. Saved identities and simulations are not live readiness. The read-only residents/patch/probe.h exchange uses a fresh challenge and pinned build, shares the mutation gate, checks adapter identity under its lease and returns the last cached request/result without consuming sequences or executing a mutation. Poisoned engines supply recorded diagnostics only; wrong builds disclose no cached bytes. kernel_patch.py probe-request/probe-decode operate on saved files and validate challenge/build/state/cache consistency; the separately documented stage 2 bridge now implements authenticated inspection dispatch, with SDK installer integration/link and live validation still outstanding.

KERNEL_CAPTURE_CORE.md documents the host-tested cooperative resident capture core: at most four existing DR0-DR3 execution slots with explicit grants on every scoped CPU, full GP register events, bounded per-CPU rings/hit budgets, and sticky ownership revocation. It installs no traps and has no live adapter. Readiness inspection capability is not a slot grant; all four slots occupied without grants means ENOSPC. Caller serialization and adapter quiescence are required; disarming logging does not prove hardware cleanup.

KERNEL_EXECUTION.md documents the nonblocking SMP coordinator and one-request polled mailbox: all-CPU park and restoration barriers, ticketed single-CPU stepping/cleanup, finite budgets, deadlines and failure holding, with replay-safe commands and an offline host codec. Tests simulate 16 concurrent CPUs; make kernel-execution-check emits a compile-only SDK object. No live rendezvous, architectural step, physical transport or hardware restoration is installed. COMPLETE records release acknowledgements, not proven target execution; a resident adapter must independently quiesce before retirement. ps5debug-NG was reviewed at 938d1a7: its process ptrace and kernel R/W are not an SMP kernel stop backend, and its PCB writer must not bypass the retired fallback guard.

DURABLE_CHECKPOINTS.md documents lib/checkpoint (usermode-only, one-shot TCP, runtime groups, fsync-before-ACK, bounded deadlines and sticky failures), host/checkpoints.py listen/ingest/summary, and common/evidence.h schema-1 288-byte records. Runs pin fresh sessions, source/build IDs, exact ELF hashes, observer/subject process identities and per-build site schemas; xapp through xeax are successive operator-reported experiments, not app stages. residents/evidence supplies preallocated per-CPU trace rings, optional full GP state, separate first-panic slots and bounded partial-write exporters. Panic-only output needs a preinitialized independent physical channel; no live panic hook, UART driver, DR/PCB/IDT/TSS change or console validation is supplied. make evidence-check SDK-builds a benign example and freestanding no-red-zone/general-register-only object. Host EOF, ShellUI death, a black display or a supplied panic record does not independently prove a kernel panic; unexported console RAM is lost at reboot.

KERNEL_PATCH_STAGE2.md documents the implemented private source overlay for pinned kstuff-lite 47da23b70685651a475d20247a3c4f2cac433eb4: tooling/prepare_kernel_patch_stage2.py exports committed sources without editing the checkout, generates a private bearer credential and source/config build pin, and verification refuses stale/mismatched inputs. The 104-byte authenticated envelope dispatches read-only probe queries only; the 176-byte shared state fits existing allocations, publishes inspection capability 1, verifies 16 existing CPU IST readbacks and pmap/site bytes, and revokes on changed state. No new IDT/TSS/PCB/debug-register writer or mutation engine is added. User page audits are not OS pins and do not prove SMP mapping lifetime. make kernel-patch-stage2 defaults to no provider; configured ELFs contain a credential and are excluded from all/bundle. make kernel-patch-stage2-check emits actual bridge/dispatch and bootstrap compile objects, not a linked resident or installer. stage2-decode validates saved public exchanges with an independent build pin and leaves present readiness/whole-kernel identity false. Full resident build, live syscall/copy/coexistence validation and current console readiness remain outstanding; no console deployment or stage 3 write validation is claimed.

KERNEL_PATCH_STAGE3.md documents the owned-cell source adapter on the same pinned resident: prepare_kernel_patch_stage2.py --stage 3 creates a separate private overlay; stage-specific verification prevents mixing stage 2 and 3 builds. The sole accepted mutation is sequence-1 EXERCISE on one resident-owned aligned eight-byte cell with exact bytes and session/build, capability 3 on its separate channel; arbitrary data/code and APPLY/REVERT remain outside this bridge. Shared nonblocking gate plus owned-cell lease, resident PREPARE/OUTCOME/COMPLETE journal, cached result before copyout, exact replay without writes and sticky quarantine protect this bounded operation. Callback pointers are cleared between per-CPU calls. Shared mappings expand within the existing allocation; original field offsets/snapshots remain unchanged. make kernel-patch-stage3 and kernel-patch-stage3-query are optional SDK exercise and strictly read-only recovery clients, provider-free by default and excluded from all/bundle. stage3-decode checks saved public evidence, fixed policy, fresh challenges and restored bytes/journal/cleanup; a saved record is not present readiness or whole-kernel attestation. Host tests/sanitizers and actual bridge/dispatch/bootstrap compile checks do not establish a full linked resident, stage 2 hardware validation or console writes. No stage 3 deployment or live restoration is claimed.

KERNEL_PATCH_RESEARCH.md separates reproducible build/owned-cell controls from the unproven exec+0xcfc12 Chain Test hypothesis. KERNEL_PATCH_BUILD.md and make kernel-patch-resident add opt-in complete resident linking and actual installer source compilation with LLVM 18. Prepare a fresh private overlay with --link-inputs: all exported source/header/assembly files, exact BearSSL/ISA-L gitlinks, generator and builder are pinned. ELF audits enforce the pinned loader relocation/import/mapping subset. Evidence records source/config and exact artifact/tool hashes; installer_linked and console_validated remain false pending SDK startup integration and hardware validation. Private outputs/configurations contain bearer credentials and must stay outside Git/public bundles. Scholarly purpose is not itself a blanket legal exemption.

Chain Test is an unvalidated repackaged PS5SX2 launch specimen. KERNEL_PATCH_EXPERIMENTS.md records the 2026-10-21 validity correction: no successful launch of the exact package was found on any firmware. Builder verification, installation, matching staging files and other titles launching do not establish package launch validity. Failures under the tested 13.60 configurations leave package validity and firmware compatibility confounded; plaintext-wide and memcpy-causal claims remain unproven. Require exact-package successful launch and an independently demonstrated working homebrew FPKG comparison before firmware attribution.

KERNEL_PATCH_EXPERIMENTS.md defines H1 transfer-fault containment, H2 application baseline observations and a future H3 remedy comparison. make kernel-patch-campaign / host/kernel_patch_campaign.py compile the actual portable core into a host experiment: 44,256 cases over APPLY/EXERCISE/REVERT, lengths 1-64, partial/error writes and short reads, with replay/quarantine checks. Saved reports pin source/compiler and preserve failed runs; known-bad disposable-core sensitivity controls verify detection. This finite adapter model and sanitizer success are not console crash-rate evidence, hardware fault containment or kernel-code patch validation. The live stage 3 bridge remains a fixed eight-byte exercise. No production core/payload change or console deployment is part of this experiment.

follower-live streams new KSTUFF_OBS ring words and prints each tracked ioctl command once, including its group byte. On firmware 13.60 a PPR mount is a pfs SM ioctl, group 0x32, not nmount. A zero nmount counter during a title launch is expected. The shared-area ioctl table lists only commands the resident recorded, so a missing group 0x32 does not prove the mount was absent. thread-probe-v3 is the read-only repeating title walker. host/stream_logger.py keeps the loader connection open with no idle timeout. Neither payload installs kstuff or writes the kernel.

KERNEL_CAPTURE_REUSE.md incorporates dated workspace OPERATING.txt and October 19 FPKG progress records: one instrumented resident per fresh Relapse, logging/emulation/resume and reader3 exports after some black-screen failures. These are not demonstrated interactive all-CPU stops or evidence of ring-fullness crashes. Historical xr15 already captured full r15/rax/frame-slot values; xff0 retained loader service while the title stayed black. Current resident identity and health require fresh evidence. Prefer one pinned resident with reviewed bounded observation windows/bookmarks; runtime configuration and application recovery remain unimplemented. Pinned kstuff rings overwrite/wrap; emptying them cannot restore ShellUI, undo skipped operations or permit another resident installation. Snapshot waits remain a candidate requiring exact-build review. Host tests cover 100 windows on 16 simulated CPUs and show drain cannot resolve failed restoration/missing CPUs. No live reset/resume adapter or reboot-free recovery is validated.
